title: Detect all project technologies
action: Before any scan or audit, detect all technologies used in the project.

title: Derive the stack from files
action: Do not ask the user which stack they use; detect it by reading the project files.

title: Step 1 — Scan root files
action: Inspect the listed root manifests to identify the language and ecosystem.

title: Step 2 — Detect framework
action: Inspect the listed configuration and dependency indicators to identify the framework.

title: Step 3 — Detect database/BaaS
action: Inspect the listed files and dependencies to identify database and BaaS technologies.

title: Step 4 — Detect deployment
action: Inspect the listed files and directories to identify deployment and CI/CD technologies.

title: Step 5 — Detect special features
action: Inspect the listed files and dependencies to identify special features.

title: Step 6 — Detect environment
action: Inspect the listed files and configuration to identify the environment.

title: Output the detected stack
action: After detection, output the language, framework, database, deployment, CI/CD, special features, environment, and loaded-category count in the shown format.

title: Activate only relevant checks
action: Activate checks only when the detected stack makes them relevant.
adaptations: No absent-stack category silently disappears: non-applicability requires evidence; otherwise the category remains pending.

title: .gitignore secret coverage
action: Verify `.gitignore` exists and contains every listed environment, key, certificate, and secrets-path pattern.

title: Append missing .gitignore entries
action: If `.gitignore` exists, append only missing required entries.
adaptations: Inventory only: do not edit `.gitignore` automatically.

title: Create missing .gitignore
action: If `.gitignore` is absent, create it from the applicable template.
adaptations: Inventory only: do not create files automatically.

title: Environment example exists
action: Verify `.env.example` or `.env.sample` exists.

title: Create placeholder environment example
action: If `.env` exists without `.env.example`, create an example containing the same keys with placeholder values.
adaptations: Inventory only: do not create or read secret-bearing configuration.

title: No real values in environment examples
action: Never include real values in `.env.example`.

title: Check tracked environment files
action: Check whether any `.env` file is tracked.

title: Classify tracked environment files
action: Classify any tracked `.env` file as a critical issue.

title: Remove tracked environment file from the index
action: Add a tracked `.env` to `.gitignore` and remove it from the Git index.
adaptations: This ledger authorizes no Git mutation.

title: Scan source for hardcoded secrets
action: Scan all source files for the listed API-key, token, service credential, JWT, and high-entropy assignment patterns.

title: Apply bounded secret-scan exclusions
action: Exclude only the listed dependency, VCS, test, spec, example, and sample paths from this pattern scan.
adaptations: Do not generalize these examples into blanket scanner exclusions.

title: Scan comments for secrets
action: Scan comments for password, secret, key, token, and API-key assignments using the listed patterns.

title: Check backup and dump files
action: Check the listed backup, dump, copy, and old-file names for secrets.

title: Verify a pre-commit secret scanner
action: Verify `.git/hooks/pre-commit` exists and performs secret scanning.

title: Create a missing pre-commit secret scanner
action: If the hook is absent, create the shown gitleaks-or-fallback hook.
adaptations: Inventory only: do not create hooks or execute embedded commands; critically assess the fallback scanner.

title: Verify gitleaks configuration
action: When gitleaks is used, verify `.gitleaks.toml` exists.

title: Create missing gitleaks configuration
action: If `.gitleaks.toml` is absent, create it from the template.
adaptations: Inventory only: do not create scanner configuration.

title: Disable production source maps
action: Verify production source maps are disabled using the applicable Next.js, Webpack, or Vite setting.

title: Scan history for secrets
action: Scan Git history for added environment, key, certificate, password, secret, API-key, or token material and classify matches critical.
adaptations: This ledger authorizes no Git or history access; the check remains a later-stage obligation.

title: Create .gitignore from the stack template
action: Use `templates/gitignore/[stack].gitignore` when creating a missing `.gitignore`.
equivalence: Repeated remediation occurrence of the `.gitignore` requirement.
adaptations: Inventory only: no file creation.

title: Append only missing .gitignore template entries
action: Add only missing template entries to an existing `.gitignore`.
equivalence: Repeated remediation occurrence of the `.gitignore` requirement.
adaptations: Inventory only: no file edit.

title: Move a hardcoded secret to environment lookup
action: Replace a hardcoded secret with an environment-variable lookup.
adaptations: Inventory only: no source edit or secret handling.

title: Separate real and placeholder environment values
action: Put the real value only in protected `.env` storage and a placeholder in `.env.example`.
adaptations: Do not acquire, display, or write secret values during this inventory.

title: Confirm before applying a secret fix
action: Obtain the authorization required by current controlling instructions before applying the secret fix.
conditions: The current authority does not already cover the action.
adaptations: Do not create an extra approval loop when current authority already covers the action.

title: Revoke or rotate a leaked credential
action: Immediately revoke or rotate a credential found in Git history.
adaptations: External credential action requires authority for that action.

title: Rewrite history manually after a leak
action: Use the shown `git-filter-repo` procedure manually to remove the leaked path.
adaptations: This ledger authorizes no package installation, Git rewrite, or force-push.

title: Notify collaborators after history rewrite
action: Notify all collaborators to re-clone after the history rewrite.

title: Record rotation status in memory-security.md
action: Update `memory-security.md` with detected secrets and rotation status.
adaptations: The controlling SKILL forbids changing assistant memory or files during this inventory.

title: Flag stale secret rotation
action: Flag any secret not rotated within `rotation_reminder_days` (default 90 days).

title: Never allow wildcard CORS in production
action: Do not configure wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` in production.

title: Validate dynamic CORS origins
action: When multiple origins are required, validate the request origin against an explicit allowlist.

title: Credentialed CORS requires a specific origin
action: When `credentials: true`, the CORS origin must not be wildcard.

title: Restrict allowed HTTP methods
action: Allow only HTTP methods the API actually uses and omit unused methods from `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`.

title: Cache CORS preflight responses
action: Configure `Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400` for the source's 24-hour preflight cache policy.

title: Search every public endpoint for rate limiting
action: Actively search all public APIs, webhooks, login endpoints, contact forms, and exports for rate limiting.

title: Apply a global API rate limit
action: Apply a global rate limit to public API traffic.

title: Apply strict limits to sensitive endpoints
action: Apply stricter limits to login, registration, OTP, and password-reset endpoints.

title: Return rate-limit headers
action: Return `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, and `RateLimit-Reset` headers.

title: Return 429 for rate limits
action: Return `429 Too Many Requests`, not 403, when a rate limit is exceeded.

title: Force HTTPS redirect
action: Redirect an insecure request to HTTPS using a trustworthy transport signal.

title: Require TLS 1.2 minimum
action: Require TLS 1.2 or newer.

title: Prefer TLS 1.3
action: Prefer TLS 1.3.

title: Disallow TLS 1.0 and 1.1
action: Never permit TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1.

title: Inspect ssl_protocols
action: Check Nginx or Apache `ssl_protocols` configuration.

title: Do not disable TLS verification
action: Do not set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`, `verify=False`, or otherwise disable certificate verification.

title: Block development ports in production
action: Block the listed development and debugger ports in production.

occurrences.sourceLabel: 13. Development Ports Not Exposed in Production

title: Do not expose database ports publicly
action: Keep PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, and Redis ports off the public internet; inspect firewall and Compose mappings.

title: Do not run the Node debugger in production
action: Do not start production Node.js with `--inspect`, especially on `0.0.0.0`.

occurrences.sourceLabel: 15. Node.js Debugger Not Active in Production

title: Limit request body size
action: Set reasonable JSON, form, and upload body-size limits.

title: Check header-size limits
action: Check server `client_header_buffer_size` or equivalent header-size limits.

title: Configure connection timeouts
action: Configure bounded request, header, body, send, and keepalive timeouts.

title: Limit connections per client
action: Limit concurrent connections per client or IP.

title: Check for default credentials
action: Scan code and configuration for the listed default credentials and classify any hardcoded credential critical.

title: Set HSTS
action: Set `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload`.

title: Set a restrictive CSP
action: Set the source's `Content-Security-Policy` directives for default, script, style, image, frame ancestors, base URI, and form action.

title: Generate a CSP nonce per request
action: Generate a cryptographically random nonce for each request.

title: Do not allow unsafe CSP script execution
action: Never use `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'`.

title: Set X-Frame-Options
action: Set `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.

title: Set X-Content-Type-Options
action: Set `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

title: Set Referrer-Policy
action: Set `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.

title: Set Permissions-Policy
action: Disable the listed camera, microphone, geolocation, payment, and USB capabilities in `Permissions-Policy`.

title: Set COOP
action: Set `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`.

title: Set COEP
action: Set `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`.

title: Set CORP
action: Set `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`.

title: Remove fingerprinting headers
action: Remove `X-Powered-By`, server-version disclosure, and `X-AspNet-Version`.

title: Require Trusted Types for script
action: Add `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` to CSP.

title: Scan DOM injection sinks
action: Scan for `innerHTML =`, `document.write()`, and `outerHTML =`.

title: Allow private-network access only when applicable
action: When explicitly required, set `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true`.
ambiguities: Private Network Access is context-dependent; candidate applicability and origin authorization remain unassessed.

title: Reject cross-site unsafe requests
action: Reject cross-site non-GET requests using `Sec-Fetch-Site` validation.
ambiguities: Clients or transports may omit `Sec-Fetch-Site`; this header check is not a complete authorization or CSRF control by itself.

title: Use SRI for CDN resources
action: Give CDN resources an integrity hash and `crossorigin="anonymous"`.

title: Flag CDN resources without SRI
action: Flag any CDN resource without an integrity hash.

title: Clear client state on logout
action: Send `Clear-Site-Data: "cache", "cookies", "storage"` on logout.

title: Set response-specific cache policy
action: Use `no-store, no-cache, private` for sensitive pages, `private, no-store` for API user data, `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for static assets, and `public, s-maxage=300` for public pages.
adaptations: Any later generalization to long or bounded caching must be recorded as an explicit adaptation, not substituted for the source literals.

title: Use a password KDF
action: Do not hash passwords with MD5, SHA-1, or SHA-256; use bcrypt with cost factor at least 12 or Argon2.

title: Require at least 14 password characters
action: Require passwords to contain at least 14 characters.

title: Block common passwords
action: Block passwords found in a top-10,000 common-password list.

title: Check breached passwords privately
action: Check passwords through the HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity API.
adaptations: External password-derived data transmission requires authority and must preserve the k-anonymity privacy design.

title: Do not rely on complexity alone
action: Never enforce uppercase, number, and symbol complexity rules alone.

title: Prevent recent password reuse
action: Prevent reuse of the last five passwords.

title: Never return passwords in API JSON
action: Never include `user.password` or another password value in an API response.

title: Verify the current password before change
action: Verify `currentPassword` before allowing a password change.

title: Prevent account enumeration messages
action: Return the same authentication failure message whether the account exists or the password is wrong.

title: Equalize authentication failure timing
action: Keep authentication failure timing equivalent with constant-time comparison where applicable.

title: Rate-limit login attempts
action: Allow at most five login attempts per IP per 15 minutes.

title: Use progressive login lockout
action: Apply progressive lockout after authentication failures.

title: Require CAPTCHA after repeated failures
action: Require CAPTCHA after three failed attempts.

title: Lock after ten consecutive failures
action: Lock the account after ten consecutive failures.

title: Alert on unusual login activity
action: Alert the user to unusual login activity.

title: Do not use security questions
action: Do not use guessable security questions; use an email link plus MFA for recovery.

title: Regenerate the session after login
action: Regenerate the session identifier after authentication.

occurrences.sourceLabel: 7. Session ID Regeneration After Login (Session Fixation)

title: Regenerate on privilege escalation
action: Regenerate the session when roles change or sudo mode begins.

occurrences.sourceLabel: 7. Session ID Regeneration After Login (Session Fixation)

title: Regenerate around OAuth
action: Regenerate the session before the OAuth redirect and after the callback.

occurrences.sourceLabel: 7. Session ID Regeneration After Login (Session Fixation)

title: Do not put WebSocket session IDs in URLs
action: Do not accept session IDs in WebSocket URLs; pass them only through secure cookies.

title: Bound session lifetime
action: Use a configurable 30-minute inactivity timeout and an absolute maximum lifetime of eight hours.

title: Set secure authentication-cookie flags
action: Set all authentication/session cookies `httpOnly: true`, `secure: true`, and `sameSite: 'strict'`.

title: Use protected cookie prefixes
action: Use `__Host-` or `__Secure-` cookie prefixes where their constraints apply.

title: Destroy all session state on logout
action: Destroy the server-side session, clear the session cookie, and clear client cache, cookies, and storage on logout.

title: Do not place tokens in URLs
action: Pass tokens through a POST body or `Authorization` header, not a URL.

title: Deploy a CSRF defense
action: Use at least one of `SameSite=Strict`, `Sec-Fetch-Site` validation, or an explicit CSRF token.

title: Verify OAuth state
action: Generate a random OAuth state value, store it server-side, and verify it at callback.

title: Use PKCE for public clients
action: Use PKCE for SPAs and mobile applications.

title: Require exact OAuth redirect URIs
action: Validate redirect URIs by exact match against an allowlist.

title: Generate strong reset tokens
action: Generate password-reset tokens with 256 bits of cryptographic randomness.

title: Store only a reset-token hash
action: Store the SHA-256 hash of a reset token rather than the token.

title: Expire reset tokens promptly
action: Expire reset tokens after 15 minutes.

title: Make reset tokens single-use
action: Invalidate each reset token after its first use.

title: Bind reset tokens to users
action: Verify that a reset token is bound to the expected user identifier.

title: Invalidate reset tokens on password change
action: Invalidate outstanding reset tokens when the password changes.

title: Hash recovery codes
action: Hash MFA recovery codes with bcrypt before storage.

title: Make recovery codes single-use
action: Invalidate each recovery code after use.

title: Generate recovery codes cryptographically
action: Generate recovery codes with `crypto.randomBytes()` or an equivalent CSPRNG.

title: Invalidate superseded recovery codes
action: Invalidate old recovery codes when new codes are generated.

title: Use a narrow TOTP window
action: Use a TOTP verification window of one step (the source's ±30-second window).

title: Invalidate used TOTP values
action: Invalidate a TOTP value after successful use.

title: Rate-limit OTP attempts
action: Allow at most three OTP attempts per minute.

title: Transmit a TOTP secret only once
action: Transmit the TOTP secret only once during setup.

title: Use an established WebAuthn library
action: Use an established WebAuthn library such as SimpleWebAuthn; never implement WebAuthn manually.

title: Require WebAuthn user verification
action: Set `userVerification: 'required'`.

title: Use an exact WebAuthn rpID
action: Set `rpID` to the exact domain rather than an overly broad parent.

title: Use a random single-use WebAuthn challenge
action: Generate a cryptographically random challenge and make it single-use.

title: Verify attestation in high-security contexts
action: Verify WebAuthn attestation in high-security contexts.

title: Maintain a passkey recovery plan
action: Maintain an account-recovery plan for WebAuthn/passkey users.

title: Mask password inputs
action: Use `type="password"` and the appropriate `autocomplete="current-password"` or `autocomplete="new-password"` value for password fields.

title: Use modern cryptographic algorithms
action: Do not use MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC4, or ECB mode; choose the listed modern primitive appropriate to hashing, symmetric encryption, or asymmetric signing.

title: Scan for deprecated cryptography calls
action: Scan for the listed `md5`, `sha1`, DES, and `aes-256-ecb` calls.

title: Use a CSPRNG for security values
action: Do not use `Math.random()` for tokens or OTPs; use `crypto.randomBytes()` or `crypto.randomInt()`.

title: Generate a random IV for each encryption
action: Generate a fresh random initialization vector for every encryption operation.

title: Store the IV with ciphertext
action: Store the initialization vector alongside the ciphertext.

title: Compare secrets in constant time
action: Use `timingSafeEqual` or an equivalent constant-time operation for tokens, hashes, and signatures.

title: Configure forward-secret TLS
action: Use ECDHE or DHE cipher suites with TLS 1.2/1.3 and avoid RSA key exchange.

title: Centralize cryptographic algorithm selection
action: Configure cryptographic algorithms in a centralized module instead of hardcoding them throughout the codebase.

title: Zero sensitive mutable buffers after use
action: Use a mutable buffer for sensitive values and overwrite the buffer after use.

title: Use initialized Node.js buffers
action: Do not use deprecated or uninitialized Buffer constructors; use `Buffer.alloc()` or `Buffer.from()`.

title: Limit user-controlled buffer allocation
action: Validate and cap a user-controlled allocation size before calling `Buffer.alloc()`.

title: Use a costed password KDF
action: Hash passwords with a salted, costed KDF such as bcrypt or Argon2id.

title: Validate expected API certificates
action: For applicable mobile or server-to-server clients, validate the trusted CA and expected server certificate fingerprint.

title: Verify critical-file integrity at startup
action: Verify the configured hashes of critical files at startup and fail closed on mismatch.
adaptations: The example's logger must not override the pinned logging-Off requirement.

title: Allowlist the JWT algorithm
action: Explicitly allowlist the expected JWT algorithm and reject `none` and weak algorithms.

title: Prevent HS/RS algorithm confusion
action: Do not accept an HMAC algorithm when asymmetric JWT verification is expected.

title: Do not trust arbitrary jku
action: Do not automatically fetch a JWT `jku`; when supported, validate it against an exact allowlist.

title: Do not trust embedded JWK keys
action: Do not use a public key supplied by the token's `jwk` header.

title: Allowlist kid values
action: Validate `kid` against known keys; never interpolate it into SQL or a filesystem path.

title: Use a strong JWT HMAC secret
action: Use at least a 256-bit random JWT HMAC secret.

title: Bound JWT lifetime
action: Use short-lived access tokens and a bounded refresh-token lifetime.

title: Keep JWT payloads non-sensitive
action: Do not put passwords, payment data, or unnecessary personal data in the readable JWT payload; keep claims minimal.

title: Support token revocation
action: Provide revocation for critical tokens, or a bounded short-expiry and refresh-token design that limits stolen-token lifetime.

title: Do not store bearer JWTs in localStorage
action: Store browser JWTs in `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies rather than `localStorage`.

title: Verify JWT audience and issuer
action: Verify `aud` and `iss` so a token for one service is not accepted by another.

title: Reject malformed token input
action: Reject an absent or non-string token before JWT verification.
equivalence: New normative detail extracted from the complete-verification template.

title: Perform complete JWT claim verification
action: Verify the explicit algorithm, audience, issuer, bounded clock tolerance, and expiration.
equivalence: Composite template occurrence of the algorithm, lifetime, audience, and issuer rules.

title: Check JWT revocation state
action: Check the token identifier against revocation state during verification.

title: Do not allow all Firestore access
action: Do not use `allow read, write: if true`; require authentication and enforce resource ownership or authorized role in Firestore rules.

title: Require Firebase Storage ownership for read and write
action: Require authentication and matching user ownership for the example Firebase Storage read/write rule.

title: Restrict the Firebase API key
action: Restrict the Firebase API key to only the required APIs.

title: Enable Firebase App Check
action: Enable Firebase App Check for production.

title: Enable Supabase row-level security
action: Enable row-level security on every applicable public table.

title: Keep the Supabase service-role key server-side
action: Never expose `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in frontend code.

title: Parameterize SQL values
action: Bind SQL values through parameters or a parameterizing ORM.
adaptations: Allowlist any user-influenced SQL structure; value binding does not secure identifiers or clauses.

title: Prevent SQL truncation
action: Validate string length before insertion and enable strict database truncation behavior.

title: Use a least-privilege database account
action: Use a dedicated application database user with only required data permissions; do not grant root, schema, or administrative powers.

title: Do not hardcode database credentials
action: Load the database connection string from protected configuration rather than code or public configuration.

title: Verify TLS for production database connections
action: Use TLS for production database connections with certificate verification enabled.

title: Do not expose database ports publicly
action: Keep PostgreSQL 5432, MySQL 3306, and MongoDB 27017 off the public internet and restrict access to authorized application servers.

title: Require MongoDB authentication
action: Require authenticated MongoDB connections.

title: Constrain MongoDB query input
action: Coerce the MongoDB email input to a primitive string and validate its email format before querying.

title: Require Redis authentication
action: Configure Redis `requirepass` or an equivalent authenticated access control.

title: Restrict Redis network binding
action: Bind Redis only to authorized private or loopback interfaces, not `0.0.0.0`.

title: Expire sensitive Redis data
action: Give every cached sensitive value a finite TTL.

title: Protect sensitive database fields at rest
action: Encrypt credit-card, SSN, passport, bank-account, and comparable sensitive fields before storage; hash passwords rather than storing plaintext.

title: Do not expose database internals in errors
action: Return generic database errors to clients rather than schema or query details.
adaptations: The detailed-logging example is subordinate to the pinned logging-Off requirement; document any visibility consequence without adding hidden logs.

title: Use least-privilege GitHub Actions permissions
action: Grant only the permissions each job needs; grant `id-token: write` only when OIDC is required.

title: Pin GitHub Actions to immutable SHAs
action: Pin each third-party Action to a specific commit SHA rather than a mutable tag.

title: Do not execute fork code with pull_request_target secrets
action: Never combine `pull_request_target` privileges with checkout and execution of untrusted fork code.

title: Keep untrusted workflow context out of shell source
action: Pass untrusted GitHub context through environment variables rather than interpolating it into a shell command.

title: Do not log workflow secrets
action: Never intentionally echo secrets in CI logs.

title: Minimize GITHUB_TOKEN scope
action: Do not request `GITHUB_TOKEN` write access unless the job genuinely requires it.

title: Expose only public Vercel variables
action: Use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix only for values intended to be public in the browser bundle.

title: Do not put secrets in vercel.json
action: Keep secrets out of committed `vercel.json`; use an authorized secret facility.

title: Configure Vercel security headers
action: Configure the required response security headers for Vercel routes.

title: Do not hardcode Cloudflare Worker secrets
action: Read Worker secrets from authorized bindings rather than source code.

title: Do not put secrets in wrangler.toml
action: Use `[vars]` only for non-sensitive values and an authorized secret binding for secrets.

title: Verify Cloudflare security settings
action: Verify applicable WAF, bot controls, rate limiting, DDoS protection, and `Full (Strict)` TLS settings.
adaptations: Dashboard access and any setting change require authorization for that external action.

title: Use least-privilege AWS IAM
action: Grant only required AWS actions on the required resources.

title: Block public S3 access
action: Enable S3 Block Public Access and ensure no bucket policy grants public access.

title: Do not embed AWS credentials
action: Use IAM roles or protected environment configuration instead of credentials in code.

title: Keep platform production secrets out of Git
action: Never commit `.env.production`; use an authorized platform secret store and verify `netlify.toml` or `railway.json` contains no secrets.

title: Maintain Dependabot configuration
action: Maintain a weekly `.github/dependabot.yml` update configuration; create it if missing.
adaptations: Inventory only: do not create or edit Dependabot configuration automatically.

title: Disable development endpoints in production
action: Disable development documentation, introspection, admin, database-console, and overly revealing status endpoints in production, or protect/minimize them as applicable.

title: Require signed commits where applicable
action: Advise enabling signed commits and the protected-branch signed-commit requirement.
adaptations: This inventory authorizes no global Git or repository-setting change.

title: Do not run the container as root
action: Run the application as a dedicated non-root user.

title: Do not bake secrets into image layers
action: Keep secrets out of Dockerfile commands and image layers; inject them through an authorized runtime secret mechanism.

title: Verify .dockerignore coverage
action: Verify `.dockerignore` excludes the listed environment, VCS, dependency, log, coverage, and test artifacts.

title: Pin base images
action: Pin each base image to a specific version or digest rather than `latest`.

title: Use a minimal compatible base image
action: Use a minimal compatible runtime image to reduce attack surface.

title: Use a multi-stage image build
action: Use a multi-stage build so build tools and artifacts do not enter the runtime image.

title: Use a read-only container filesystem
action: Run with a read-only root filesystem and only the required `tmpfs` writable paths.

title: Drop container capabilities
action: Drop all capabilities, add back only those required, and set `no-new-privileges:true`.

title: Do not use privileged containers
action: Do not use `privileged: true` unless a separately justified requirement makes it unavoidable.

title: Avoid host networking
action: Use bridge or an explicit custom network rather than `network_mode: host`.

title: Limit container resources
action: Set CPU and memory limits and reservations.

title: Define container health checks
action: Define a bounded container health check.

title: Do not publish database ports
action: Keep database ports off the host and accessible only through the internal container network.

title: Scan container images
action: Run an authorized vulnerability scan of container images.

title: Verify production image signatures
action: Require signed production images and verify them through the authorized trust mechanism.

title: Disable GraphQL introspection in production
action: Disable GraphQL introspection and playground access in production.

title: Limit GraphQL query depth
action: Reject GraphQL queries deeper than the configured safe maximum.

title: Limit GraphQL query complexity
action: Reject GraphQL queries whose calculated complexity exceeds the configured safe maximum.

title: Authorize sensitive GraphQL fields
action: Enforce authentication and role authorization in every sensitive resolver.

title: Mask GraphQL errors in production
action: Return a generic GraphQL error in production rather than internal details.

title: Limit GraphQL batching
action: Disable batched GraphQL HTTP requests or enforce a bounded batch size.

title: Use WSS in production
action: Do not use plaintext `ws://` WebSockets in production; use `wss://`.

title: Validate WebSocket origins
action: Validate the WebSocket upgrade `Origin` against an explicit allowlist.

title: Authenticate each WebSocket connection
action: Authenticate every WebSocket connection.

title: Validate every WebSocket message
action: Parse each WebSocket message safely and validate it against a field-specific schema before handling it.

title: Rate-limit WebSocket messages
action: Rate-limit messages per WebSocket connection or client and disconnect abusive peers.

title: Terminate idle WebSocket connections
action: Use ping/pong and bounded timers to terminate idle or unresponsive connections.

title: Verify webhook HMAC signatures
action: Verify each webhook HMAC over the raw body with a timing-safe comparison before processing.

title: Make webhook delivery idempotent
action: Track a stable webhook event identifier and do not process the same event twice.

title: Authenticate and scope SSE subscriptions
action: Require authentication for SSE and send only events scoped to the authenticated user.
